chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Saeed, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not perform Sajdah upon the Qir (bitumen/asphalt), nor upon the Sarouj (cement/construction material).
ai.seo_question: What materials are prohibited for performing Sajdah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) specifies that Sajdah on Qir (bitumen) and Sarouj (construction mortar) is disliked, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that prostration should occur on natural, pure earth rather than processed or mixed materials. This ruling underscores the emphasis on humility and connection to the primordial earth during worship, distinguishing between permissible substrates and those deemed less ideal due to their artificial composition.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Amro Bin Saeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Neither perform Sajdah upon the asphalt, nor upon Al-Sarouj (construction material like cement)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Idris and others have narrated Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn ’Isma‘il from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn Sa‘id who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must not perform Sajdah (prostration) on graves and on a mix of lime and construction compound.’”
